data.exact_reserve_text: Reassessment of claims outstanding on underwriting years 2015 & prior (2017 - 2014 & prior) resulted in an improvement of GBP 44.6m (2017 - GBP 55.9m).

prior_year_events.impact_description: Large marine hull fire at German shipyard; significant loss which impacted the 2014 year of account; expected substantial reinsurance recovery and affected reserving for prior years.

named_events.loss_description: Fire at a German shipyard destroying a luxury mega-yacht; described as a very large marine hull physical damage claim; syndicate expects substantial reinsurance recoveries; contributed to development on earlier years.
Reserved at a combined $21.6m (reported in USD) as at reporting date; expected to give meaningful claims for property lines.
Previously estimated gross ~$125m and net ~$86m; at 31.12.2018 reserved losses reported as ~$123m gross / ~$83m net (figures reported in USD).
One of the 2018 natural catastrophe events expected to cause a relatively modest loss, but likely the largest among 2018 hurricanes for the syndicate.
Notable large risk impacting Marine War reserving class referenced in underwriting commentary.

data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2018 were GBP 701.094m. During 2018 the syndicate carried out a reassessment of claims outstanding for underwriting years 2015 and prior which resulted in an improvement (release) of GBP 44.6m (approximately 6.4% of opening gross reserves). The release is attributed to favourable claims development and specific favourable outcomes including settlements on large energy claims being below previously held reserves, alongside broader back-year run-off. Named large losses (e.g. Project Sassi from 2014) and 2018 catastrophe activity (California wildfires, hurricanes) are discussed elsewhere in the report and have influenced class-level reserving and reinsurance recoveries.
raw_causal_phrases: Reassessment of claims outstanding on underwriting years 2015 & prior (2017 - 2014 & prior) resulted in an improvement of GBP 44.6m (2017 - GBP 55.9m).
favourable run-off of the back years contributed 81% to the result
we have seen some back year case reserve improvements; most notably two large Energy losses settled at levels below our reserves; as well as general favourable development across most classes.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from balance sheet 'Claims outstanding' (prior year column). Prior year development (-44.6m) taken from note '6. CLAIMS OUTSTANDING' which explicitly states an improvement of GBP 44.6m for underwriting years 2015 & prior; the note does not explicitly label the figure 'gross' but is presented in the claims outstanding context and thus treated as gross. Some named event amounts are reported in USD in the text (e.g. $21.6m for Camp & Woolsey) and have not been converted to GBP; where event amounts are only quoted in USD they are left null here. Claims development triangle is available (gross) and used for verification; RITC and portfolio movements are present elsewhere in the report and may affect interpretation of development for certain years.
